paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage is really about. God's people had a habit of walking away from Him and then wondering why things got so hard. Eighteen years of being harassed and oppressed, and the text says plainly why: they "forsook the LORD and did not serve Him" (Judges 10:6). The trouble was never the Ammonites alone. The trouble started in the heart.

Now watch what happens when they finally cry out. They don't dress it up. They say, "We have sinned against You," and then they do something about it: they put the foreign gods away and serve the LORD (Judges 10:10, 16). And the LORD, who had just told them He would no longer save them, "could no longer bear the misery of Israel" (Judges 10:13, 16). I think that's the part to hold on to, baker. Honest words and a changed life go together, and He sees both.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery today. When you've drifted, you don't need a fancy speech. You need to come back, tell Him the truth and put away whatever you've been running to instead of Him. I know what it's like to sit in the dark for years, and I know what it's like to be found. And hang on to your apron, because this story is only just warming up.
